method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)' (retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required)), 19 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that "eviQ content should not be hosted on external sites", and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9) 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)' (published 17 March 2026), 11 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13186868). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. The S1 source file concatenates two eviQ protocol pages (https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3836 and https://www.eviq.org.au/p/291), each under a header line naming its URL. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the SEOM–TTCC 2025 head and neck cancer guideline (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, paraphrased and hash-anchored), for radiotherapy dosing, cisplatin-ineligible options, induction, perioperative pembrolizumab, first-line choice by PD-L1 CPS, platinum-refractory and later lines, and follow-up. S1 claims and anchors are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Plan and review treatment with a multidisciplinary team;** combined-modality treatment is common and the after-effects need joint management. Look for a clinical trial.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nutrition risk is high:** a dietitian should see every patient first, and a speech pathologist should assess speech and swallowing before treatment starts.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definitive chemoradiation with three-weekly cisplatin** is for unresectable locally advanced HNSCC with performance status 0 to 2. Avoid it with grade 2 or worse neuropathy or significant hearing loss or tinnitus.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Regimen:** cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, 3 cycles given during radiotherapy.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Why cisplatin:** in the Intergroup trial, adding high-dose cisplatin to standard radiotherapy improved survival (projected 3-year survival 37% versus 23%), at the cost of more grade 3+ toxicity (89% versus 52%).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aim for a cumulative cisplatin dose of at least 200 mg/m2;** efficacy seems to depend on total dose delivered.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weekly versus three-weekly cisplatin is debated.** One prospective study found low-dose weekly treatment inferior; preliminary conCERT data suggest weekly 40 mg/m2 is non-inferior for two-year locoregional control (52.6% v 47.4%).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other eviQ options** are weekly cisplatin chemoradiation and carboplatin with fluorouracil chemoradiation; the cetuximab chemoradiation protocol is marked superseded.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy (S2):** IMRT or VMAT, which cut xerostomia without losing control, at 70 Gy given as 35 fractions across 7 weeks, or 65–66 Gy as 30 fractions across 6 weeks [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2 on concurrent cisplatin:** 100 mg/m² on days 1, 22 and 43 for a total above 200 mg/m² [I, A]; weekly schedules have not been shown non-inferior [II, B]. Benefit falls in patients older than 70, so select carefully and support throughout.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Cisplatin-ineligible (S2):** cetuximab bioradiotherapy (400 mg/m² on day −8, then 250 mg/m² weekly with radiotherapy) is an alternative [I, A], although it is inferior to concurrent cisplatin. Adding immunotherapy to chemoradiation has not improved outcomes.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Induction chemotherapy (S2):** TPF (cisplatin 75 mg/m², docetaxel 75 mg/m² and fluorouracil 750 mg/m² a day by 96-hour infusion, given three-weekly) is the regimen of choice [I, A] for fit patients with good organ function; it lowers metastasis without a clear survival gain. Follow it with cisplatin chemoradiation where possible, as cetuximab is not non-inferior.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider salvage neck dissection** when the primary has responded completely but PET–CT still shows nodal disease 12 weeks after treatment [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Resectable locally advanced disease with PD-L1 CPS 1 or more: perioperative pembrolizumab** (2 cycles before surgery and 15 in total afterwards) improved event-free survival over surgery then (chemo)radiotherapy in a phase III trial; FDA approval came in June 2025 and EMA approval in October 2025 [I, A]. Induction chemotherapy before surgery is not supported [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Kidneys and hearing:** use measured GFR for the first cisplatin dose when eGFR is under 60 (especially above 50 mg/m2), give pre-hydration, and arrange audiometry if hearing symptoms appear.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fluorouracil:** DPYD genotyping has been MBS-funded since 1 November 2025. An antidote works well for overdose or overexposure if given within 96 hours. Monitor for cardiac toxicity, particularly with pre-existing heart disease.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Who:** first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic HNSCC arising more than 6 months after any platinum chemotherapy, with ECOG 0 or 1.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Regimen:** pembrolizumab 200 mg, cisplatin 100 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 4,000 mg/m2 (1000 mg/m2 a day by pump over 96 hours) every 21 days for 6 cycles, then pembrolizumab alone (or 400 mg every 42 days) until progression or intolerable toxicity; KEYNOTE-048 capped pembrolizumab at 35 cycles.

claims.claim: **If full-dose cisplatin is unsuitable, substitute carboplatin.** For PD-L1 CPS of 1 or more, pembrolizumab on its own is a reasonable alternative.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **KEYNOTE-048:** pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy beat cetuximab-based EXTREME for overall survival (median 13.0 v 10.7 months; HR 0.77), with benefit in CPS 1 or more (HR 0.65) and CPS 20 or more (HR 0.60). PFS was not improved overall.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Toxicity was similar to EXTREME** (grade 3+ in 85% v 83%); hypothyroidism was the commonest immune effect (16% with chemotherapy) and pneumonitis caused a death.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'eviQ head and neck SCC protocols: 3836 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma recurrent or metastatic cisplatin fluorouracil and pembrolizumab' (v.4, last reviewed 31 May 2024) and 291 'Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma locally advanced definitive cisplatin (three weekly) chemoradiation' (v.9, last reviewed 14 April 2023)', retrieved 23 September 2026 (protocol 3836 review due 30 June 2026, now overdue; 291 reviewed as required), https://www.eviq.org.au/medical-oncology/head-and-neck, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **S2 first-line choice by PD-L1 CPS (platinum-naïve or recurrence more than 6 months after platinum, good performance status):** CPS 20 or more, pembrolizumab alone is preferred when symptoms and disease burden are low, or pembrolizumab with platinum–fluorouracil when a response is needed; CPS 1–19, pembrolizumab with platinum–fluorouracil is preferred, with pembrolizumab alone if chemotherapy is unsuitable; CPS under 1, EXTREME (platinum–fluorouracil with cetuximab), or TPEX (cisplatin–docetaxel–cetuximab) if fluorouracil cannot be used [I, A].
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Performance status 2:** paclitaxel with cetuximab (ERBITAX), a single chemotherapy drug or cetuximab alone [III, C]; evidence for pembrolizumab here is limited, so use it case by case. Performance status 3 or worse: supportive care only.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Progression or recurrence within 6 months of cisplatin: do not rechallenge with a platinum doublet.** For good performance status, nivolumab is preferred whatever the PD-L1 result [I, A]; pembrolizumab alone may be considered when TPS exceeds 50%. If anti-PD-1 therapy is contraindicated or unsuitable (high, fast-moving disease), use ERBITAX or single-agent chemotherapy.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Second line depends on first line:** after pembrolizumab alone, EXTREME or TPEX if platinum-fit (ERBITAX if PS 2 or platinum-unfit); after pembrolizumab with platinum–fluorouracil, ERBITAX; after EXTREME or TPEX, nivolumab [I, A] or a single agent (taxane or capecitabine). Beyond that, single-agent taxanes or antimetabolites by fitness; offer trials.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Follow up for at least 5 years:** 40–60% of locally advanced cancers recur, mostly within 2 years, and second primaries (lung, urinary tract, head and neck) arise at 2–4% a year. Examine with flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy, investigate persistent pain or new neck lumps, offer smoking and alcohol cessation support, and do not use serum tumour markers.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Head and Neck Cancer Group (TTCC) (Arrazubi, Iglesias et al.), Clinical and Translational Oncology 28(6) (doi 10.1007/s12094-026-04240-9), 'SEOM–TTCC clinical guidelines for the treatment of head and neck cancer (2025)', published 17 March 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13186868/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pseudo-progression happens in about 5%:** if the patient seems to be benefiting, consider continuing and repeating the scan 4-6 weeks later before calling progression. Radiation recall can occur after a long radiotherapy course.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immune-related adverse events can start early, worsen fast, appear after stopping, and can kill** (e.g. myocarditis, myositis, encephalitis, pneumonitis). Monitor proactively, teach self-monitoring, and treat promptly with interruption, specialist input and corticosteroids.

claims.claim: **Use expert judgement before immunotherapy** in significant autoimmune disease, organ transplant recipients, past viral hepatitis, or previous lung irradiation.

claims.claim: **Monitoring:** screen for hepatitis in everyone before a checkpoint inhibitor; check thyroid function (and consider cortisol) every 4-6 weeks on treatment and every 12 weeks afterwards as indicated.
